description: We are Team RockIT, a group of students from Bukidnon State University joining the NASA Space Apps Challenge! With a mix of developers, designers, pitchers, and leaders on board, we combine our different perspectives to analyze NASA open data. We are excited to experiment, learn together, and turn simple ideas into a practical project for the competition.
summary:
EMBER (Emergency Monitoring & Burn-zone Early Response) is a unified web platform that harmonizes multi-sensor NASA FIRMS satellite fire data (MODIS and VIIRS) into a centralized interactive map, settlement proximity alert system, and historical burning calendar.

To address fragmented satellite records characterized by incompatible spatial resolutions, disparate confidence scales, and redundant alarms from overlapping orbital passes, EMBER processes raw telemetry through a five-step geospatial harmonization pipeline hosted on Vercel. The platform polls live active fire data via the NASA FIRMS Web Map Service (WMS) integration; standardizes geographic coordinates; normalizes MODIS numeric percentages and VIIRS categorical flags into uniform severity tiers (Low, Medium, and High); deduplicates overlapping detections within a 375-meter radius; and executes idempotent upserts to eliminate duplicate records on repeat passes while integrating wind vectors to project downwind drift zones.

By translating complex orbital telemetry into an intuitive risk map, distance-based settlement proximity alerts, structured safety checklists, and historical burn calendars, EMBER enables local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Offices (DRRMOs), land managers, and residents to distinguish routine agricultural burns from hazardous wildfires and mitigate fire risks prior to escalation.
details: EMBER (Emergency Monitoring & Burn-zone Early Response) is a unified web application hosted on Vercel that bridges raw orbital telemetry and ground-level response by harmonizing multi-sensor NASA FIRMS satellite fire data from Suomi NPP, NOAA-20, Terra, and Aqua into a centralized interactive map, settlement proximity alert system, and hot spot calendar. Developed by Team RockIT for non-technical responders, the platform operates through a five-step pipeline that polls live active fire feeds via the NASA FIRMS Web Map Service (WMS), standardizes coordinates, normalizes MODIS numeric percentages and VIIRS categorical flags into uniform severity tiers, deduplicates overlapping detections within a 375-meter radius, and executes idempotent upserts while integrating wind vectors to map downwind drift zones. By eliminating redundant alerts from overlapping orbital passes, EMBER provides local Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Offices (DRRMOs), land managers, and residents with actionable intelligence—combining distance-based proximity alerts, wind-drift projections, plain-language hot spot calendars, and structured safety checklists covering what to do, what to bring, and what to prepare—to empower communities to rapidly distinguish routine agricultural burns from dangerous wildfires and mitigate fire hazards before escalation.
